ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint space-time scale schedule for discrete video generation
PROPOSAL: Train a 2B-parameter bitwise autoregressive transformer on 2 million captioned clips at 256p, where each next-scale step predicts a coarse-to-fine token map for the whole clip and the spatial and temporal resolutions grow together. Compare it with a variant that predicts scales frame by frame and conditions on earlier frames. Both models share one discrete tokenizer, 16 frames per clip and the same data order. Evaluate text-to-video with VBench and FVD on UCF-101 and MSR-VTT over 2,048 generated clips, and record generation latency per clip on one accelerator type.
CONTROLS: A raster-order next-token model at equal parameter count; a spatial-only scale schedule with full temporal attention at the finest scale; an ablation of the temporal growth rate; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The joint schedule should lower FVD by a few points and roughly halve latency compared with frame-by-frame prediction, with motion smoothness gaining most. It could fail if coarse early scales cannot represent fast motion, visible in flicker on high-dynamics prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal scale ladders for discrete video generation
PROPOSAL: Train a 2B-parameter bitwise autoregressive transformer on 2 million captioned clips at 720p, splitting each clip into coarse motion codes and fine appearance codes that are predicted in successive scales. Retrain the same recipe from 5 seeds and on 4 ladder depths, then score each checkpoint on VBench, FVD with UCF-101 and MSR-VTT, and CLIP similarity over the whole test prompt list. Latency is measured for each checkpoint on one accelerator type, using 16 frames per clip and identical data order.
CONTROLS: A raster-order next-token model at equal parameter count; a ladder with motion and appearance codes merged; a ladder with fixed depth and random code order; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Deeper ladders should lower FVD with diminishing returns and keep latency near flat. The comparison could fail if motion codes carry little information at the coarsest scale, which would leave motion smoothness equal to the merged variant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initialising a discrete video tokenizer from an image tokenizer versus training from scratch
PROPOSAL: Build a causal 3D discrete tokenizer with a 2 million entry bitwise codebook in two ways: extend the weights of a pretrained image tokenizer along the temporal axis, or train from random weights on 4 million clips at 256p. Train each for the same number of steps and track reconstruction PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on WebVid and Kinetics-600 validation clips every 10,000 steps, along with codebook utilisation. Then freeze each tokenizer and train a 1B generator on its tokens to see whether reconstruction quality carries through to generation FVD.
CONTROLS: A frame-independent image tokenizer applied per frame; a tokenizer initialised from image weights with temporal layers frozen; an equal-step schedule so that wall-clock differences do not confound; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Image initialisation should reach the scratch model's PSNR in under half the steps, but the final gap on motion-heavy clips should narrow. It could fail if image weights bias the codebook toward static textures, visible in low utilisation and blurred motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a discrete video tokenizer from an image tokenizer
PROPOSAL: Train a causal 3D discrete tokenizer with a 2 million entry bitwise codebook on 4 million clips at 256p by distilling features from a pretrained image tokenizer, with a temporal compression of 4 frames per token column. Evaluate reconstruction PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on WebVid and Kinetics-600 validation clips at every checkpoint in a schedule of ten snapshots, for 5 seeds each. Freeze every snapshot and train a 1B generator on its tokens to measure generation FVD, so that the whole trajectory of the tokenizer can be tied to downstream quality.
CONTROLS: A frame-independent image tokenizer applied per frame; a tokenizer trained with no distillation term; a tokenizer with an adversarial loss only; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Distillation should reach competitive PSNR early and then plateau, while generation FVD tracks reconstruction up to a saturation point. It could fail if the image features carry no motion information, in which case rFVD would stay close to the per-frame baseline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Keyframe memory with windowed attention for long video contexts
PROPOSAL: Extend a 1B discrete autoregressive video model to minute-long clips by attending only to a local window of the latest 8 frames plus a memory of keyframes chosen by token novelty. Train on 500,000 long clips from a public movie dataset with 256p tokens. Measure temporal consistency by DINO feature similarity between distant frames, subject identity retention with a face and object tracker, and VBench quality, and report memory and latency growth with video length.
CONTROLS: Full-history attention on clips short enough to fit, as an upper bound; a pure sliding window with no memory; a memory of uniformly spaced keyframes; ablation of the memory size; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Novelty-chosen keyframes should keep identity retention within a few points of full attention while keeping latency nearly linear in length. It could fail on scenes with repeated returns to earlier content, where uniformly spaced memory may match it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical context compression for long autoregressive video
PROPOSAL: Extend a 1B discrete autoregressive video model to minute-long clips by compressing older frames into coarse summary tokens at three levels of detail, with an attention window over the latest 8 frames. Train on 500,000 long clips from a public movie dataset at 256p with 20 different compression rates, and retrain the full pipeline on 5 seeds. Measure DINO feature similarity between distant frames, identity retention with a face and object tracker, and VBench quality, together with memory and latency growth for videos from ten seconds to ten minutes.
CONTROLS: Full-history attention on clips short enough to fit; a pure sliding window; a learned pooling of old frames with no coarse levels; ablation of the number of levels; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Coarser summaries should hold identity retention while trimming memory, up to a compression rate beyond which consistency collapses. The result could be a null one if summary tokens are ignored by the attention layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency and quality of a discrete autoregressive video model against diffusion baselines at 720p
PROPOSAL: Train a 7B-parameter next-scale autoregressive model for text-to-video at 720p on 10 million clips, using a bitwise tokenizer with 16x spatial and 4x temporal compression, and compare it head to head with an open diffusion video model of similar size. Report VBench dimensions, a blind human preference study with 300 prompts and 5 annotators each, and wall-clock latency for 5-second clips at batch sizes 1 and 8 on one accelerator type with matched numerical precision and an optimised attention kernel.
CONTROLS: Open diffusion video model checkpoints with their default sampler and with a distilled few-step sampler; a next-token raster autoregressive model; an equal-token-count ablation so that sequence length does not favour either family.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The autoregressive model should be several times faster at similar VBench totals and be slightly behind on fine detail. It could fail if bitwise tokens limit small-text rendering, visible in the human study.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quality and speed profile of a discrete autoregressive video model against diffusion baselines
PROPOSAL: Train a 7B-parameter next-scale autoregressive model for text-to-video at 720p on 10 million clips, using a bitwise tokenizer with 16x spatial and 4x temporal compression, and put it next to an open diffusion video model of similar size on the standard benchmark suites. Report VBench dimensions, a human preference study with 300 prompts and 5 annotators each, and latency for clips of 2, 5 and 10 seconds at light and heavy batch loads on three accelerator types with matched numerical precision, repeating each timing 20 times.
CONTROLS: Open diffusion video model checkpoints with their default sampler and with a distilled sampler; a next-token raster model; a sequence-length-matched ablation; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The autoregressive model should be several times faster in all settings with comparable quality totals. The latency advantage could shrink on the oldest accelerator if memory bandwidth dominates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Video extrapolation by conditioning on a discrete prefix
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 2B discrete autoregressive video model so that it continues a given clip: the first 2 seconds are tokenised and used for conditioning, and the model produces the next 8 seconds scale by scale. Train on 1 million clips from a public stock footage collection with a mixture of text-only and prefix-conditioned examples. Score continuation on held-out clips with FVD, drift in colour histograms across time, and motion continuity measured with optical flow between the last prefix frame and the first generated frame.
CONTROLS: A diffusion-based extension baseline using overlapping windows; a model trained only on text-to-video and prompted with the prefix at inference; ablation of the prefix length; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Prefix conditioning should cut flow discontinuity in half against the inference-only prompting and match overlapping windows on FVD at lower latency. It could fail if colour drift grows with each extension, visible in the histogram curves.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extrapolating video from a discrete prefix with long continuation horizons
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 2B discrete autoregressive video model so that it continues a given clip: a prefix of 2 seconds is tokenised and the model produces up to 60 seconds scale by scale. Train on 1 million clips from a public stock footage collection with a mixture of text-only and prefix-conditioned examples, then evaluate on four held-out sets using eight prefix lengths and 5 sampling temperatures. Score FVD, colour histogram drift across time, and optical flow continuity at each seam.
CONTROLS: A diffusion-based extension baseline using overlapping windows; a model trained only on text-to-video and prompted with the prefix; a no-prefix control; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Longer horizons should show a steady rise in drift but stable flow continuity at the first seam. The model could fail beyond 30 seconds if errors accumulate in the coarse scales.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-round video generation that follows successive instructions
PROPOSAL: Build a training set of 200,000 chained editing dialogues in which each round supplies a new instruction and the model continues the clip, then fine-tune a 3B discrete autoregressive video model on it using a causal mask over rounds. At test time run dialogues of 3, 5 and 8 rounds. Judge instruction following per round with a video-language model scored against human labels on 500 dialogues, scene consistency across rounds with DINO similarity, and FVD per round.
CONTROLS: A single-instruction model re-prompted with the whole history in text; a model that regenerates from scratch each round; ablation of the history length kept in context; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Instruction following should stay above that of re-prompting after the fifth round and consistency should decay gently. It could fail if later rounds contradict earlier ones, which the per-round scores expose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Round-by-round instruction following in long interactive video
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 3B discrete autoregressive video model on 200,000 synthetic dialogues, where an instruction-writing video-language model proposes a new edit for each round and the clip grows by a few seconds. Mask later rounds from earlier ones so that training stays causal. At test time run dialogues of up to 20 rounds with 6 instruction styles and 4 history lengths, each from 5 random seeds. Judge instruction following per round with a video-language model scored against human labels on 500 dialogues, scene consistency with DINO similarity, and FVD per round.
CONTROLS: A text-only history baseline that re-prompts a single-instruction model; a model that restarts generation at each round; a context-length ablation; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Instruction following should decline slowly with the round index and depend little on the style. The approach could fail if history length matters more than the instruction itself.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bitwise vocabulary size for discrete video tokens
PROPOSAL: Train 600M-parameter next-scale video generators whose bitwise tokenizers use codebook widths of 16, 24 and 32 bits per code, on 1 million clips at 256p. Track reconstruction rFVD for each tokenizer, then generation FVD, VBench quality and training loss for each generator. Examine how the logit layer for bitwise prediction behaves when the width grows, by recording per-bit accuracy by scale.
CONTROLS: A standard index-based vocabulary of 65,536 entries; a bitwise model with factorised bit groups; matched parameter and step counts; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Wider codes should improve rFVD with diminishing returns beyond 24 bits while per-bit accuracy drops at the finest scale. It could fail if the generator cannot exploit the added detail, leaving generation FVD flat.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Wide bitwise codebooks for discrete video tokens at high resolution
PROPOSAL: Train 600M-parameter next-scale video generators whose bitwise tokenizers use codebook widths from 12 to 48 bits per code in six steps, on 1 million clips at 720p. Track reconstruction rFVD for each tokenizer, then generation FVD, VBench quality and training loss for each generator, from 4 seeds. Study the bitwise prediction layer by recording per-bit accuracy for each scale and each width on 3 test sets.
CONTROLS: A standard index-based vocabulary of 65,536 entries; a bitwise model with factorised bit groups; a model with a continuous latent head; matched step counts; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Wider codes should improve rFVD and then saturate, with per-bit accuracy falling at the finest scale. The study could fail to separate widths above 32 bits at equal training length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image and video mixture ratio in a single discrete generator
PROPOSAL: Train a 4B discrete next-scale transformer that serves text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video from one set of weights, using 100 million images and 20 million clips. Compare 3 mixture schedules: a fixed ratio, image-heavy pretraining followed by video-heavy training, and a curriculum that raises video proportion over time. Evaluate GenEval and DPG-Bench for images, VBench for videos, and first-frame fidelity for image-to-video.
CONTROLS: Separate image-only and video-only models of equal size; a model trained with a joint loss but no timestep for the temporal axis; ablation of the curriculum slope; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The curriculum should match image-only quality within two points on GenEval and exceed the fixed ratio on VBench. It could fail if video training erodes image fidelity, which GenEval exposes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture schedules for a unified discrete image and video generator
PROPOSAL: Train a 4B discrete next-scale transformer that serves text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video from one set of weights, using 100 million images and 20 million clips. Compare twelve mixture schedules built from four starting ratios and three slopes, each with 3 seeds, and evaluate GenEval and DPG-Bench for images, VBench for videos, and first-frame fidelity for image-to-video at 5 checkpoints along training.
CONTROLS: Separate image-only and video-only models of equal size; a joint-loss model with no temporal axis; a schedule with random task order; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Most schedules should land within a point of each other on quality. The comparison could fail to show a reliable winner if differences stay below seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Controlling error accumulation in long discrete video generation
PROPOSAL: Test whether corrupting previous frame tokens at training time reduces drift during long rollouts. Train a 2B discrete autoregressive video model on 2 million clips at 256p, replacing a random fraction of tokens in the preceding frames with samples from the model's own predictions. Roll out videos of 30 seconds and measure the rise of FVD and of the DINO similarity gap with respect to the first frame over time, using 1,000 prompts.
CONTROLS: The same model trained on clean history only; a model with token dropout in history but no self-predictions; an ablation of the corruption rate; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Self-prediction corruption should reduce the growth rate of FVD by about a third in the last 10 seconds. It could fail if the corrupted history lowers short-term quality, visible in early-frame FVD.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-generated history for stable long video rollouts
PROPOSAL: Test whether training on the model's own generated history reduces drift during long rollouts. Train a 2B discrete autoregressive video model on 2 million clips at 256p in four rounds; after each round regenerate the history for 50 percent of the clips and mix it into the next round, with six rates of replacement and four seeds. Roll out videos of 120 seconds with 1,000 prompts and plot FVD and the DINO similarity gap to the first frame for every setting.
CONTROLS: The same model trained on clean history only; a model with token dropout in history; a model trained on history from a different generator; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Self-generated history should flatten drift beyond one minute. It could fail if the model collapses to repeated content after several rounds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining recipe for a 12B discrete video model at 720p
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 12B-parameter discrete next-scale model for text-to-video at 720p on 50 million clips with a bitwise tokenizer, using a staged schedule: 256p for the first 60 percent of tokens, 480p for the next 25 percent and 720p for the remainder. Evaluate with VBench at 720p, FVD on Kinetics-600, and a human study with 200 prompts, and report loss curves per scale with the final latency for a 5-second clip.
CONTROLS: A model trained at 720p from the start for the same number of tokens; a 3B model on the same schedule to measure scaling; a diffusion model of similar size for external reference.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Staged training should reach the final quality of direct 720p training with markedly fewer high-resolution tokens. It could fail if the lower stages leave resolution-specific artefacts in the fine scales.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Resolution curriculum for a 12B discrete video model
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 12B-parameter discrete next-scale model for text-to-video at 720p on 50 million clips with a bitwise tokenizer, running 9 resolution curricula that differ in when 480p and 720p begin, each with 3 seeds. Evaluate each with VBench at 720p, FVD on Kinetics-600 and a human study of 200 prompts, and report loss curves per scale with the final latency for a 5-second clip.
CONTROLS: A model trained at 720p from the start; a 3B model on the same schedules; a diffusion model of similar size for reference; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The curricula should converge to similar quality, with later 720p starts giving the best compute trade-off. The comparison could fail to show differences if scores stay inside noise.
